FIXTURE ORCHARD HANDBOOK
TEST FIXTURE ONLY. Synthetic text written for software tests; it is not part of any real corpus.

1. Planting Schedule
Saplings in the fixture orchard are planted between the third and fifth week of the planting
season. Each sapling receives 12 litres of water on the day it is planted.

Approved sapling varieties:

1. Red Fixture Apple
2. Golden Fixture Pear
3. Blue Fixture Plum

2. Pruning
Pruning happens once per year after the last frost. Branches thicker than a thumb are cut with a
saw, never with shears.

2.1 Ladder Safety
Ladders are permitted in the orchard only when a second worker holds the base of the ladder.

2.2 Ladder Storage
Ladders are not permitted in the orchard overnight and must be returned to the tool shed.

§ 3 Harvest Limits
A picker may fill at most 40 crates per shift. Damaged fruit is placed in the compost bin, not in
the crates. The harvest supervisor checks the crate count at the end of every shift. Crates are
stacked no more than five high. Stacks taller than five crates must be split before the cart
leaves the row. The cart driver confirms the stack height before moving. Fruit picked after
sunset is recorded separately. Late fruit is stored in the cool room until the next morning.

4. Tool Shed
Before leaving the shed, each worker must:
1. Clean the blades.
2. Hang every tool on its hook.
3. Sign the tool register.
